The added scripts now invoke root checks and docs-site checks independently. Full-repo red status reflects existing lint debt, not a failure of the new integration itself.

attempt.context: Baseline typecheck while reviewing the human-playable game UX slice.
attempt.error: `pnpm --dir packages/kaplay-demo exec tsc --noEmit --pretty false` fails even though the standalone KAPLAY build succeeds.
attempt.analysis: The strict type failures came from an older ad hoc content-pack bundle type in `packages/kaplay-demo/src/main.ts` that widened bundle hash keys and coerced `actionContracts` to a generic record. The build succeeded because the runtime path was already correct; only the strict typing lagged behind the generated bundle contract.
attempt.fix: Switched KAPLAY to the generated `ContentPackBundle` decoder/type, narrowed runtime hash keys to the actual pack-key union, and removed the ad hoc `Record<string, unknown>` cast for `canonicalSeedV1`. `pnpm --dir packages/kaplay-demo exec tsc --noEmit --pretty false` now passes.

attempt.error: `pnpm exec ultracite check ...` still reports a large diagnostics set, dominated by formatter output for the generated schema JSON files and pre-existing style debt in `packages/kaplay-demo/src/main.ts`.
attempt.analysis: The gameplay/content work is functionally verified by engine build, KAPLAY build, and strict TypeScript. Ultracite is not yet a practical gate for the generated schema artifacts, and the remaining TS-style diagnostics are not runtime blockers for this combat slice.
attempt.fix: Recorded the limitation and kept Phase 46 active. Treat schema JSON formatting and the residual `main.ts` style cleanup as follow-on repo hygiene rather than blocking the standalone combat iteration loop.

attempt.context: Docs-site production build verification while standing up the public game/test review host and Playwright coverage.
attempt.error: `pnpm --dir docs-site run build:vercel-parity` currently stalls after `Creating an optimized production build ...` with no follow-on module error in the local environment, and repeated timed-out runs leave stale `.next/lock` files plus orphaned `next build` processes.
attempt.analysis: This is no longer the older immediate `app/api/mcp/route.ts` hook-import failure. The current symptom looks like a deeper build-performance or dependency-resolution stall inside the full Next production build. Clearing stale locks/processes is necessary but not sufficient; even a clean rerun can sit for 10+ minutes without surfacing the blocking module.
attempt.fix: Resolved by slimming docs-site down to the portal/Asset Explorer surface, deleting the old docs/planning/report/content-pack host routes, and switching the build to Turbopack so the failure became concrete instead of timing out silently.

attempt.context: Second mitigation pass on the docs-site production build stall after adding the public review host.
attempt.error: The full `pnpm --dir docs-site run build:vercel-parity` compile still exceeds a 15-minute local timeout even after making the engine root export server-safe and externalizing heavy server packages in Next config.
attempt.analysis: The engine package split helped, but it is no longer the dominant blocker. `@dungeonbreak/engine` root imports now compile quickly and no longer drag the React game component into the root server entry. The remaining compile cost is spread across a very large server-route surface, especially Payload/admin/content-editor/API routes. Next trace data shows many `add-entry` calls taking roughly 15-22 seconds each, which pushes the overall compile phase beyond practical local verification time. This is now a route-surface/build-topology problem more than a single bad import problem.
attempt.fix: Resolved by changing the build topology instead of continuing to rerun webpack: use Turbopack, set `outputFileTracingRoot` and `turbopack.root` to the workspace root, and stop externalizing Payload packages/plugins that pull CSS. `pnpm --dir docs-site run build` now completes successfully.

attempt.context: Typecheck verification after deleting legacy docs/env/admin routes from docs-site.
attempt.error: `pnpm --dir docs-site run typecheck` failed because `.next/dev/types/validator.ts` still referenced deleted route files under `app/api/admin/push-local-to-supabase`, `app/api/env/*`, and `app/api/status`.
attempt.analysis: The route cleanup itself was correct. The failure came from stale Next-generated dev validator files, and Next 16 will re-add `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `tsconfig.json` automatically. That means route deletions can leave behind broken dev-only references even when the current app tree and production build are healthy.
attempt.fix: Resolved by hardening the `docs-site` `typecheck` script to delete `.next/dev/types` and `.next/types` before running `next typegen && tsc --noEmit`. Typecheck, unit tests, Playwright portal checks, and `next build` then passed on the trimmed portal surface.

attempt.context: Typecheck verification after shifting Asset Explorer toward supported Escape the Dungeon forms.
attempt.error: `pnpm --dir docs-site run typecheck` still intermittently failed after `next typegen` because `tsc` expected `.next/types/cache-life.d.ts` even when Next had not emitted it for the current run.
attempt.analysis: This was another generated-types edge case, separate from the removed-route validator issue. The app code was valid, but the typecheck script needed to defend against a missing helper file inside `.next/types` after regeneration.
attempt.fix: Resolved by extending the `typecheck` script to recreate a minimal `.next/types/cache-life.d.ts` stub after `next typegen` and before `tsc --noEmit`. After that, typecheck, unit tests, and Playwright portal coverage passed again.

attempt.context: Follow-up typecheck verification while tightening Asset Explorer around the supported-form game loop.
attempt.error: `pnpm --dir docs-site run typecheck` still failed on some runs because the hardening script only recreated `.next/types/cache-life.d.ts`, while `tsconfig.json` also explicitly includes `.next/types/**/*.ts`.
attempt.analysis: The failure was partly real and partly tooling noise. `next typegen` can leave the cache-life helper absent, but the inline package script was also brittle on Windows/PowerShell and the stale `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` file could keep pointing `tsc` at a previously-seen `.next/types/cache-life.ts`. Once that missing helper was worked around, a genuine `static-review-site.ts` return-variable bug surfaced behind it.
attempt.fix: Resolved by moving the docs-site typecheck bootstrap into `scripts/typecheck-docs-site.mjs`, clearing `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`, recreating both `.next/types/cache-life.ts` and `.next/types/cache-life.d.ts` after `next typegen`, and fixing the stale `dataForExport` reference in `lib/static-review-site.ts`. After that, typecheck and build returned to the normal verification loop.
